title: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
tagline: Understand how people think, feel, and behave, and learn to study it scientifically.
overview:
The Bachelor of Arts in Psychology introduces you to the scientific study of the mind and behavior, and trains you to ask good questions about people and answer them with evidence. After a broad introduction to the field, you build the research and statistical skills that every psychologist relies on.

Across the major you study the discipline's core areas, including development, social, cognitive, biological, and clinical psychology, then choose electives in topics such as positive psychology, forensic psychology, and the psychology of technology. Your degree culminates in a two-term senior sequence in which you propose, conduct, and report an original study.
outcomes: Describe the major concepts, theories, and findings across the core areas of psychology.
Design and critique research using appropriate methods, measures, and ethical safeguards.
Analyze and interpret behavioral data using descriptive and inferential statistics.
Apply psychological principles to personal, social, and organizational problems.
Communicate psychological knowledge clearly in writing and speech, following APA conventions.
Recognize the role of culture and diversity in human behavior and in psychological science.
